text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000208's 99215 billing is concentrated on low-complexity patients, a pattern consistent with upcoding, but the few returned charts support the billed level and are too thin to settle it.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern is the main concern. The 99215 share runs well above the all-provider share in every complexity band, and the gap is widest for patients with 0 or 1 conditions. Many sampled low-complexity 99215s carry routine diagnoses such as rash (R21), upper respiratory infection (J06.9), urinary tract infection (N39.0) and follow-up (Z09), as in C0113906, C0114635, C0113888 and C0114847. Against that, all three documented 99215s were supported, including C0113982, a 0-condition abdominal pain visit documented at high MDM and 51 minutes, and only 1 of 12 data-reviewed notes lacked a test line on the claim. That is weak counter-evidence, because records cover under 2% of claims, so the documentation is too thin to judge. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215s with routine diagnoses, then check whether the notes support high MDM or are templated or cloned to match the billed level."}
